## Design note

Point-and-squirt in any weather. Instant dual-clutch shifts and AWD launches make it brutally quick to 100 km/h for its power, and it is the most forgiving fast car in the roster. The price is a front-heavy chassis that understeers when pushed and a ceiling the rear-drive cars break through on open roads.

## How this car breaks

Modern UHSS cell and long crumple rails make it one of the safest cabins on the list; frontals crush the nose but rarely the occupants. The rear coupling and prop shaft run under the floor, so heavy kerb or sill strikes can kill drive to the rear. Plastic everywhere outside the cell: cheap to bend, cheap to fix.

- manufacturer spec-class data for 2010s AWD 2.0 T hot hatches

- engineering tables (tire radius, ride frequency, caliper hydraulics)

All values are class-typical figures for the archetype, rounded; no single real vehicle is reproduced.

## Inertia

Box approximation about the CG, scaled for mass concentration (`k < 1`: mass near the centre, e.g. mid-engine; `k → 1`: mass at the ends):

```
I_roll  = k_r · m·(W² + H²)/12
I_pitch = k_p · m·(L² + H²)/12
I_yaw   = k_y · m·(W² + L²)/12
```

| pitch | 2523 | 0.90 | 2270 |

## Engine

2.0 L DOHC I4, single turbo, direct injection, street spec (hybrid turbo, remap), plateau 1800-5500 rpm. Street spec (2026-10 rebalance, `STREET_SPEC_W_PER_KG`): the class-typical 2010s 2.0 T curve (~110 kW/L, electronically flattened plateau as owner dynos show) scaled ×1.48 for ≈ 220 W/kg — under the 240 W/kg target on purpose, so AWD launches do not put it past the exotic to 160 km/h; curb trimmed 1500 → 1430 kg.

## Drivetrain

6-speed dual-clutch, on-demand clutch-pack rear coupling (95 % front until the fronts slip 5 %, then up to 50 % rear), open diffs with brake-based torque vectoring (assist). Layout **on-demand AWD, 95 % front with the coupling open, up to 50 % rear once the fronts out-spin the rears by 5 %**; front diff: open; rear diff: open. Clutch capacity 1.40 × peak torque = 790 N·m. Shift time 0.08 s.

| Gear | Ratio | Overall | km/h @ redline |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3.46 | 12.63 | 60 |
| 2 | 2.15 | 7.85 | 97 |
| 3 | 1.45 | 5.29 | 143 |
| 4 | 1.10 | 4.02 | 189 |
| 5 | 0.87 | 3.18 | 238 |
| 6 | 0.71 | 2.59 | 292 |

Final drive 3.65, reverse 3.00. Speeds use the driven-wheel loaded radius 0.309 m.

## Suspension

Springs from ride frequency, `k = m_s·(2πf)²` with sprung corner mass `m_s = axle load/2 − unsprung`; dampers `c = 2ζ·√(k·m_s)`, ζ = 0.30 bump, rebound = 1.5 × bump.

| Axle | m_s | f | Wheel rate k | Bump c | Rebound c | Travel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Front | 423 kg | 1.80 Hz | 54200 N/m | 2870 N·s/m | 4300 N·s/m | 0.15 m |
| Rear | 275 kg | 1.90 Hz | 39200 N/m | 1970 N·s/m | 2960 N·s/m | 0.16 m |

Anti-roll bars from a roll-gradient target of 2.2°/g with 55% of roll stiffness at the front. Roll arm h − h_rc = 0.424 m (roll centres 0.08 m F / 0.12 m R). Required total K_φ = m·g·arm/φ = 160812 N·m/rad; springs give k·t²/2 = 63796 F / 44665 R N·m/rad; bars supply the rest as `arb_n_per_m = K_bar/t²` = **10500 F / 12100 R N/m** (clamped at ≥ 0). Resulting gradient 2.2°/g, front share 55%. Bump stops 170000 N/m.

Alignment: camber -0.8° F / -1.3° R, toe +0.00° F / +0.20° R (+ = in), caster 7.0°.

## Brakes

Full-pedal line pressure 100 bar.

- Front: 340 mm disc, pistons per side 60 mm → A = 28.3 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 145 mm, pad μ = 0.42: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.42·100 bar·28.3 cm²·0.145 m = **3444 N·m**
- Rear: 310 mm disc, pistons per side 41 mm → A = 13.2 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 130 mm, pad μ = 0.4: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.4·100 bar·13.2 cm²·0.130 m = **1373 N·m**

ABS ceiling: caliper capacity 3444 / 1373 N·m exceeds 1.5 × the front lock torque on this car's tire (peak μ 1.20), which `wp_vehicle`'s ABS cannot modulate (it releases to a fraction of the commanded torque, so an oversized caliper keeps the wheel locked). Both axles scaled by 0.94 → **3230 / 1290 N·m**. Remove when 02's ABS modulates relative to lock torque.

Lock check at 1 g on μ = 1 (load transfer m·a·h/L): front needs 1795 N·m/wheel (capacity 1.80×), rear needs 455 N·m/wheel (capacity 2.83×).

`wp_vehicle` gives the axle `bias_front` favours its full `max_torque_*` and scales the other by (1 − b)/b, so `max_torque_*` holds the caliper capacity per wheel and `bias_front` acts as the proportioning valve: the rear is trimmed to the same lock margin as the front (ideal rear = T_f · lock_r/lock_f = 819 N·m), never boosted above its caliper capacity. Rear capacity exceeds that, so `bias_front` = T_r/(T_r + ideal) = **0.612** → delivered 3230 N·m front / 818 N·m rear per wheel at full pedal. Handbrake 1100 N·m per rear wheel.

## Steering

Ratio 13.6:1. Kerb-to-kerb turning circle 10.9 m → outer-front path radius 5.34 m, rear-axle-centre radius 3.88 m → mean road-wheel lock δ = atan(L/R) = **0.596 rad (34.2°)** (outer 29.5°, inner 40.2° at full Ackermann; `ackermann_frac` 0.60). Rack speed 1.7 rad/s.

## Damage lattice (`data/lattices/lindwurm_4t.json`)

271 nodes, 1778 beams, 8 detachables, 21 component mounts.

- Generated with `gen-lattice --id lindwurm_4t --profile hatch --width 1.8 --length 4.28 --height 1.44 --wheelbase 2.63 --mass 326.6 --car-mass 1484.5 --clearance 0.13 --front-overhang 0.9 --strength 1.0` (22% of vehicle mass in the lattice; strength from durability class 3).
- Era `2010s`: gen-lattice's default HSS passenger cell kept as is.
- Steel hood: 105 hood beams aluminum → mild_steel.
- Detachables: steel bumpers ×2.3 break impulse / ×4 mass; steel hood ×1.4 / ×1.6.
- Luggage bay: 13 Cabin nodes behind the rear seatback (y < -1.21 m, rear axle +0.10 m) relabelled FrameRear — the passenger cell ends at the seatback, as on a real two-box body.
- Transverse engine: gearbox mounted on the left end of the engine block (gen-lattice places it in the tunnel at the firewall, as for FR).
